name: Alphatec Holdings, Inc.
business: ATEC designs and sells spine surgery implants, instruments, neuromonitoring and EOS imaging systems to spine surgeons and hospitals in the US and abroad.

events.what: No CEO, CFO or acquisition event in window; only a director retirement and 2026 equity plan approval
Incumbent Chairman and CEO appointment (outside window, for tenure only)

street.gap_assumption: Management 18% adjusted EBITDA margin in 2027 vs VA FY2027 consensus EBITDA margin 18.53% (calendar FY, Baba label equals company year). The street sits 52.5 bps ABOVE the target; hitting exactly 18% on consensus revenue would be 2.8% below consensus EBITDA.

evidence_of_progress.note: Q1 2026 VA EBITDA margin 10.8% vs 6.2% (+458 bps); Q2 2026 company adjusted EBITDA margin 17%, +420 bps (Koning, doc 128921). VA has not loaded Q2 2026 actuals; LTM uses VA Q3 2025 to Q1 2026 plus company-reported Q2 2026 ($36M on $214M). Margin expansion is real and already in estimates; the 4-month revision is +3.2% and 12-month +4.8%.

disqualifier_reason: Margin target already reflected in consensus (FY2027 consensus 18.53% vs 18% target, gap -52.5 bps), and no leadership change or acquisition in the 18-month window (Miles CEO since 2018-03-06, Koning CFO on every call).
verdict: Cheap and with a dated 18% 2027 EBITDA margin target, but long-tenured management and the street already models above the target; not a GXO setup.
open_questions: Is the share-price drawdown about revenue (EOS and per-case pricing) rather than margin, and does the $1B 2027 revenue goal hold?
Will management issue a post-2027 long-range plan with a higher margin target, which would reopen the gap?
Does net debt near 3.6x LTM EBITDA (data_comps) constrain reinvestment?
